plants.name: Aster novi-belgii
plants.description: A clump-forming perennial native to eastern North America with daisy-like flower heads featuring yellow centers and numerous narrow petals. It is a vital late-season nectar source for migrating monarch butterflies and native bees.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to autumn (August to October)
plants.location: Eastern North America; widely cultivated in temperate gardens in Europe and Asia
plants.funFact: The name Aster comes from the Greek word for 'star'. Asters were once burned in ancient times to drive away serpents.

plants.name: Colchicum autumnale
plants.description: A bulbous perennial that produces goblet-shaped flowers in autumn, long after its leaves have died back. The blooms emerge directly from the ground without foliage, giving it the nickname 'naked ladies'.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early to mid autumn (September to October)
plants.location: Meadows and woodlands of Europe and North Africa; cultivated in temperate gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: Every part of the plant is highly toxic because it contains colchicine, a compound that is also used in medicine to treat gout and in plant breeding to induce chromosome doubling.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A large, graceful tree with fern-like foliage that bursts into clouds of trumpet-shaped blue-violet flowers before the leaves fully emerge. It carpets streets and parks with fallen purple blossoms.
plants.bloomingSeason: Spring in the Southern Hemisphere (September to November)
plants.location: Native to South America; widely planted in South Africa (Pretoria), Australia, and Argentina
plants.funFact: In Pretoria, South Africa, over 50,000 jacarandas turn the city purple each spring, and there is a local saying that a jacaranda blossom falling on your head brings good luck.

plants.name: Osmanthus fragrans
plants.description: An evergreen shrub or small tree with clusters of tiny, intensely fragrant flowers that smell of apricots and peaches. It is cherished in East Asian gardens and cuisine.
plants.location: Native to China and Japan; grown in warm temperate and subtropical gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: In China, the Mid-Autumn Festival is associated with osmanthus, and its blossoms are used to make cakes, teas, wine, and sweet syrups.
